- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after recent spikes; reduce peak values by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope and add downward bias to later periods.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is consistently above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% in next 5–7 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–4% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.3 → +0.6), apply smoothing to forecast curve to avoid oscillation.
